about: Which functions each SAS SQL dialect of the SQL Editor supports and which are pushed down to SingleStore. procsql: PROC SQL on a SAS/ACCESS to SingleStore library (implicit pass-through); fedsql: PROC FEDSQL on that library; cas: FedSQL in CAS on a SAS SpeedyStore caslib. Edit by hand or re-verify with scripts/sas_functions.py --verify; scripts/sas_functions.py --table regenerates the README table.

sources.access_map: SAS/ACCESS to SingleStore's own SQL function map: LIBNAME option SQL_FUNCTIONS_COPY= (default list) and SQL_FUNCTIONS=ALL (extended list), dumped on SAS Viya (Zeus) 2026-10-27. Option docs: SAS/ACCESS for Relational Databases: Reference, SQL_FUNCTIONS= / SQL_FUNCTIONS_COPY= LIBNAME options (https://documentation.sas.com/?docsetId=acreldb).
sources.fedsql: SAS FedSQL Language Reference (https://documentation.sas.com/?docsetId=fedsqlref): functions, SELECT (LIMIT/OFFSET), identifiers, A High-Level Comparison of PROC SQL and FedSQL.
sources.cas: FedSQL Programming for SAS Cloud Analytic Services (https://documentation.sas.com/?docsetId=casfedsql): supported statements (SELECT, CREATE TABLE AS, DROP TABLE), implicit pass-through.
sources.procsql: SAS SQL Procedure User's Guide (https://documentation.sas.com/?docsetId=sqlproc) and SAS/ACCESS for Relational Databases: Reference, "SQL Pass-Through Facility" / "Passing Functions to the DBMS Using PROC SQL" (https://documentation.sas.com/?docsetId=acreldb).
sources.verified: Run in the Workspace's SAS session (scripts/sas_functions.py --verify): the statement ran or not, and the Pushdown verdict (PROC SQL sastrace, FedSQL _method plan + driver trace, CAS method=true plan).

notes: PROC SQL: what SAS/ACCESS passes is its SQL function map (access_map: 'default' = passed, 'all' = only with the LIBNAME option SQL_FUNCTIONS=ALL); COUNT / SUM / AVG / MIN / MAX and SQL operators are always passed. The runs confirm the map; a function SingleStore doesn't get makes SAS read the rows (verdict 'pulled' / 'partly').

FedSQL: the SingleStore driver sends most SAS functions by name (e.g. INTNX, COMPRESS, LEFT, SUBSTR) and this cluster (SAS SpeedyStore) ran them in SingleStore; pushdown is judged from the driver trace (DRIVER_TRACE=SQL): PUT() only sent the column.

FedSQL in CAS on a SAS SpeedyStore caslib: 'yes' = the method=true plan shows the whole query pushed down ({Push Down}); 'partly' = the SAS Embedded Process did part of it (aggregates: grouping/ordering pushed, the Agg stage in CAS); 'no' = CAS did it (e.g. a TODAY() / CURRENT_DATE filter).
A different SingleStore cluster (without SAS SpeedyStore) or a newer SAS/ACCESS can change these results: re-run scripts/sas_functions.py --verify.
